The whole integration

<div data-wandroz="panel" data-address="Westerstraat, Amsterdam" data-modules="safety,schools,parks" data-theme="meridian"></div>
  1. You pass an address you already store — no new data entry.
  2. Wandroz resolves it to the official neighbourhood polygon and returns the rating.
  3. It renders in your colours, your corner radius, your name. "Powered by Wandroz" stays.
  4. Modules are set per account, not per page.

The snippet shows the intended shape of the integration. It is a prototype for the conversation, not a live embed.

Jordaan — the safety module in full

9,048
recorded crimes per 100,000 residents, 2025
0.5×
of the Amsterdam wijk average
1,763
registered crimes in 2025

What it means. Jordaan is central, busy and full of bars, and still records half the city's average rate. Central does not mean elevated here.

What it does not mean. The rate is against registered residents, not footfall. A nightlife area can read high without being risky to walk through. Read it as a comparison between areas of one city, not a per-visit probability.

Every bar is a real neighbouring wijk. Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde is the Red Light District — 4,345 residents against the whole city's night out, which is what 6.3× measures.

Sources
  • CBS (Statistics Netherlands) — registered crimes per wijk, 2025, with CBS 2025 population.
  • Gemeente Amsterdam — official wijk boundaries, 110 zones, api.data.amsterdam.nl.
  • Live page: wandroz.com/amsterdam/jordaan
  • CBS publishes no time-of-day breakdown, so no day/night split is shown for Amsterdam. Wandroz splits day and night only where the source supports it — London does.

What is real, and what is not

Left on the page deliberately. It is what a mobility buyer checks first.

Live Real Wandroz data

  • The map — the gemeente's own wijk polygons, drawn from the same coordinates the site publishes.
  • Every figure and every bar — CBS 2025 registered crimes and CBS 2025 population, per wijk.
  • The ratings — all eight areas shown, published now on wandroz.com.
  • The caveat — taken from the live page, not written for this deck.
  • Coverage — 65 cities, 22 countries, 2,000+ rated areas.

Concept Not built yet

  • Schools, commute, transport, essentials, parks, lifestyle, family fit — no data behind them today.
  • Shown as configured but empty slots on purpose. No commute time, school, ranking or count is invented anywhere here, because none exists.
  • The embed snippet, the three brand themes and the portal chrome are illustrative. The rent is set-dressing.
  • Which module ships first is the conversation we want with you.
